problem:
Title: Direction Angle of 2D Vector in Terms of Arctangent

Let $\mathbf a$ be a [[Definition:Vector Quantity|vector quantity]] embedded in a [[Definition:Cartesian Plane|Cartesian plane]] $P$ expressed in [[Definition:Component of Vector in Plane|component form]] as:
:$\mathbf a = x \mathbf i + y \mathbf j$

Let $\theta$ denote the [[Definition:Direction|direction]] of $\mathbf a$.

Then:
:<nowiki>$\theta = \begin{cases} 
\map \arctan {\dfrac y x} & : x > 0 \\
\map \arctan {\dfrac y x} + \pi & : x < 0 \text{ and } y \ge 0 \\
\map \arctan {\dfrac y x} - \pi & : x < 0 \text{ and } y < 0 \\
\dfrac \pi 2 & : x = 0 \text{ and } y > 0 \\
-\dfrac \pi 2 & : x = 0 \text{ and } y < 0 \\
\text{undefined} & : x = 0 \text { and } y = 0
\end{cases}$</nowiki>

where:
:$\arctan$ denotes the [[Definition:Real Arctangent|real arctangent function]], defined on the [[Definition:Open Real Interval|real interval]] $\openint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$
:$\theta$ is conventionally measured from the [[Definition:Positive Direction|positive direction]] of the [[Definition:X-Axis|$x$-axis]] in the [[Definition:Half-Open Real Interval|interval]] $\hointl {-\pi} \pi$.
